title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1LC0RE_1RA1LD_1LA1LC_1RF0RA_---0LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1LC0RE_1RA1LD_1LA1LC_1RF0RA_---0LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves three crossings the run uses and the situations that lead to a halt (kernel), and no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide); the C simulator finds no halt in 109 steps.

What it does. The head sweeps the whole tape, which is made of the three-cell words 011, 110, 100 and the pair 01, mixed with longer blocks of 1s. Going right, A turns 011 into 100; going left, C turns 110 into 011 and passes 01 unchanged. The mixture has no visible order.
Where a halt would come from. Only F reading a 0 halts; F is entered from E reading a 0, so E>0 0 halts. In 2·108 steps F always reads a 1.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 20,561 cells have been visited and 14,319 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.39). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.521).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: A turns each 011 into 100 going right (three steps a copy); C with a 1 ahead crosses 01 blocks unchanged (four steps a copy) and turns 110 into 011 (three steps a copy) going left.

claims.title: The halting situations
claims.text: E>0 0 halts after one step, B>1 0 0 after two, A>0 1 0 0 after three: two 0s in a row in the wrong place.

claims.title: F never reads a 0 in 2·10<sup>8</sup> steps
claims.text: In the first 2·10<sup>8</sup> steps the machine is in state F 5,702,121 times, every time on a 1: the halting transition F0 is never close to firing in a way the run shows.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. NGramCPS with n ≤ 10 and window CTL with K ≤ 7 leave it open.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine sweeps a tape made of a few three-cell words, rewriting them on every pass, and the words come in no visible order. This page runs it in your browser.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 20,561 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

Going left, C with a 1 ahead turns each 110 into 011:
(Lean: walk_A, walk_C110, walk_C01.) Between such runs the head meets other words and does more complicated things; that is where the content changes.

sections.heading: Two 0s in the wrong place
html: Only F reading a 0 halts. E moving right enters F, so E reading a 0 with another 0 after it halts:
F is entered 5.7 million times in the first 2·108 steps, always on a 1.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.39). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.521).
After 109 steps the tape spans 20,561 cells (4,796 left of the start, 10,186 right), with a density of 1s of 0.696.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: Two-sided bouncer whose tape is made of the short words 011, 110, 100 and 01 in no visible order; the sweeps rewrite one word into another. Open.
